statement:
A geometric sequence has first term $a$ and common ratio $r$, where $a$ and $r$ are positive integers and $r>1$.

The sum of the first $n$ terms of this sequence is denoted by $S_n$. It is given that the terms of the sequence satisfy
$$S_{30}-S_{20}=kS_{10}$$
for some positive integer $k$.

What is the smallest possible value of $k$?
solution:
Using the sum formula $S_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$,
$$S_{30}-S_{20}=\frac{a(r^{30}-1)-a(r^{20}-1)}{r-1}=\frac{a(r^{30}-r^{20})}{r-1}.$$

The condition $S_{30}-S_{20}=kS_{10}$ gives
$$\frac{a(r^{30}-r^{20})}{r-1}=k\cdot\frac{a(r^{10}-1)}{r-1},$$
so (multiplying by $r-1$ and dividing by $a$)
$$r^{30}-r^{20}=k(r^{10}-1).$$

Factorising the left side, $r^{20}(r^{10}-1)=k(r^{10}-1)$. Since $r>1$, $r^{10}-1\ne0$, so $k=r^{20}$.

As $r$ is a positive integer greater than $1$, the smallest possible $r$ is $2$, giving the smallest $k=2^{20}$.

The answer is **B**.
